findings.title: ES384 and ES512 tests sign with a P-256 key, so they never test their own curves.
findings.body: The constructor creates one key pair with `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC")` and the default size, which is P-256 on current JDKs. All three tests use that key. `testES384` and `testES512` therefore produce 32-byte r/s values that are zero-padded to 48 or 66 bytes. The P-384 and P-521 signatures the test names promise are never created. In particular the ES512 case never builds a DER sequence longer than 127 bytes. That is the only case that uses the long-form length code in `ASN1Encoder.writeLength` and `ASN1Decoder.readLength`, so that code goes untested. Fix: generate a key pair per algorithm with the matching curve, for example `kpg.initialize(new ECGenParameterSpec("secp384r1"))` for ES384 and `secp521r1` for ES512.

findings.title: Startup no longer fails when several server crypto providers are on the classpath; a tie is now picked silently.
findings.body: The old code threw `IllegalStateException` when more than one `CryptoProvider` was found. That stopped a FIPS deployment from starting if a non-FIPS provider had been bundled by mistake. Now `DefaultCryptoProvider`, `FIPS1402Provider` and `WildFlyElytronProvider` all return `order() == 200`. If two of them are on the classpath, the sort is stable, so whichever one `ServiceLoader` returns first wins. The only trace is a debug log line. For example, with `keycloak-crypto-default` and `keycloak-crypto-fips1402` both on the classpath, a server meant to run in FIPS mode can quietly use the non-FIPS BouncyCastle provider. The fix: keep the ordering, but still throw when the top two providers have the same `order()`, and log the ignored lower-priority providers at info or warn level.

findings.title: New abstract `order()` method breaks every existing `CryptoProvider` implementation outside this PR.
findings.body: `CryptoProvider` is a public SPI loaded through `ServiceLoader`. Adding `order()` as an abstract method means any implementation not updated in this PR stops compiling: custom or third-party providers, the separately released keycloak-client copy, and any test providers. An old binary that is still loaded throws `AbstractMethodError` when `detectProvider` sorts the list. I can't see from here whether other implementations exist in the repository. A default method keeps compatibility and lets providers override it.
